Operator
Hello, ladies and gentlemen. Thank you for standing by for the Q4 and fiscal year 2024 Earnings Conference Call for XPeng Inc. At this time, all participants are in listen-only mode. After management's remarks, there will be a question and answer session. Today's conference call is being recorded. I will now turn the call over to your host, Mr. Alex Xie, Head of Investor Relations, Capital Markets of the company. Please go ahead, Alex.
Alex Xie
Head of Investor Relations, XPeng
Thank you. Hello, everyone, and welcome to XPeng's Q4 and Fiscal Year 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Our financial and operating results were issued by our newswire service early today and available online. You can also view the earnings press release by visiting the IR section of our website at ir.xiaopeng.com. Participants on today's call from our management will include Co-founder, Chairman, and CEO, Mr. He Xiaopeng, Vice Chairman and President, Dr. Brian Gu, Vice President of Corporate Finance and EV Projects, Mr. Charles Zhang, Vice President of Finance and Accounting, Mr. James Wu, and myself. Management will begin with prepared remarks and the call will conclude with a Q&A session. A webcast replay of this conference call will be available on the IR section of our website.
Before we continue, please note that today's discussion will contain forward-looking statements made under the Safe Harbor provisions of the US Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. Forward-looking statements involve inherent risks and uncertainties. As such, the company's results may be materially different from the views expressed today. Further information regarding these and other risks and uncertainties is included in the relevant public filings of the company as filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission. The company does not assume any obligation to update any forward-looking statements except as required under applicable law. Please also note that XPeng's earnings press release and this conference call include the disclosure of unaudited GAAP financial measures as well as unaudited non-GAAP financial measures.
XPeng's earnings press release contains a reconciliation of the audited non-GAAP measures to the unaudited GAAP measures. I will now turn the call over to our Co-founder, Chairman and CEO, Mr. He Xiaopeng. Please go ahead.
He Xiaopeng
Co-founder, Chairman, and CEO, XPeng
大家好，我是何小鹏。在2024年的第四季度，我们达成了各项的关键目标，交付量达到了九万一千五百零七台的新高。我们的汽车的毛利率连续六个季度改善，并且在下半年自由现金流超过了四十亿。我相信这充分验证了小鹏在规模化、体系化以及战略执行能力的蜕变。进入到2025年，我们连续两个月成为了造车新势力的交付量冠军，也成为了表现最稳健的车企之一。我相信行稳才能致远。今年我会专注进一步提高小鹏汽车在体系能力，在用户的产品能力，在整个AI跟整车综合的技术能力，以及商业化能力和全球化能力的多个维度的提高。Hello, everyone, I'm He Xiaopeng.
In Q4 2024, we achieved significant milestones, including a record 91,507 vehicle deliveries in a single quarter, six consecutive quarters of improving vehicle margins, and over CNY 4 billion in free cash flow in the H2 of the year. These results highlight our significant progress in scaling, organizational improvement, and strategic execution. As we move into 2025, XPeng has topped monthly deliveries among China's emerging EV companies for two consecutive months, demonstrating our robust momentum. I believe that the key to achieving long-term goals lies in steady progress. This year, I'll dedicate myself to further enhancing XPeng's organizational capacity, user-centric product development, AI and automotive technology, commercialization, and globalization.
那么在上一个季报的AI科技日，我分享了未来的十年的汽车行业是AI的时代。在2025年，AI大模型将会为自动驾驶带来颠覆性体验的观点。而今天，在今年前三个月在中国，我们看到了在AI技术上取得了突破性的进展，更让我坚信小鹏在整个物理世界的AI大模型的战略跟技术路线的正确性。我们训练了数百亿参数规模的云端基础模型的模型，我们采用了上亿公里的真实的驾驶数据进行预训练。我相信这是中国在自动驾驶领域史无前例的模型参数量跟数据量。那么在此之上，我们会通过强化学习，提升模型的泛化能力跟处理长尾场景的能力，通过蒸馏、剪枝、量化技术部署在车端模型，并且使整个模型的精度提升超过一倍。In our last earnings call and AI tech day, I emphasized that the next decade in the automaking industry will be the era of AI, and by 2025, advanced AI models will revolutionize autonomous driving.
The AI advancement led by China in Q1 of this year has only strengthened my conviction. I'm now more confident than ever in XPeng's strategy and technology roadmap for AI large model in the physical world. We've developed a cloud-based foundational model that boasts tens of billions of parameters, leveraging over 100 million kilometers of real driving data for pre-training. This marks an unprecedented scale of model parameters and data volume in the field of autonomous driving in China. To further enhance the model's generalization capabilities and its ability to manage long-tail scenarios, we employ reinforcement learning techniques. We then implement the model in vehicles applying distillation, pruning, and quantization techniques, and have successfully boosted the model's accuracy by over 100%.
在今年一月份的时候，中国的DeepSeek-R1在数字世界的AI大语言模型是取得了非常大的成功。那么很有趣的是，这跟小鹏在自动驾驶的技术路线多个角度是不谋而合的。我们看到大模型正在不同的产业上进行跨界的融合，而小鹏也正在和不同领域卓越的AI科技公司一起在探索这些科技的边界。那么这让我非常的兴奋，我相信AI会驱动汽车产业在下一个数年里面就会产生巨大的变革，包括加速实现L3甚至L4的无人驾驶。那么同时我也看到智能汽车正在与具身智能融合的发展，智能汽车很有可能是人形机器人的前序，未来的智能汽车也一定也是具身智能的汽车。那么这一个十年，我的目标是将小鹏汽车打造面向全球的AI汽车公司，成为全球用户喜爱的智能的科技品牌。In January 2025, DeepSeek-R1 made significant strides in large language models, advancing AI capabilities in the digital realm.
Much of its technology roadmap resonates with ours. I'm thrilled to see that large models are integrating in various industries, and XPeng is exploring the frontier of technology together with leading AI tech companies from different fields. I truly believe AI will transform the automotive industry in a few years' time, speeding up the development of L3 and L4 autonomous driving. Additionally, I see a growing trend of smart vehicles and embodied AI evolving together, and smart vehicles may pave the way for humanoid robots. I'm confident that all future smart cars will be embodied AI vehicles.
[Company Representative] (XPeng)
Company Representative, XPeng
My goal for this decade is to build XPeng into an AI empowered global automotive company and a smart technology brand cherished by users worldwide.
He Xiaopeng
Co-founder, Chairman, and CEO, XPeng
我们正处在从汽车的电动化时代过渡到AI智能化时代的周期。所以如果说今年是AI agent应用的元年，那么小鹏汽车研发的AI汽车和人形机器人，我相信是物理世界AI最大的两个应用。我认为领先的AI企业要具备从云端模型到端侧模型，到整车EEA和架构，到芯片，到数据闭环的新一代的软件硬件的全栈资源，并且要叠加数据迭代的自闭环能力。所以小鹏今年会规模量产自研的图灵芯片，目前进展非常的顺利，我们会同时应用于汽车、飞行汽车和人形机器人，也可以同时用于全球化全场景的快速部署。那么图灵芯片叠加全栈的软硬件资源，会让小鹏汽车充分发挥端侧的scaling law的优势。我们相信我们不仅模型的架构领先行业一代，而且部署到车端的有效参数规模会高出行业数十倍，这在下一步会让小鹏与对手拉开显著的代际差距。我相信在今年的下半年，小鹏会在中国率先实现L3级别智能驾驶的软件能力跟体验，并且之后L3级别的智能驾驶会让用户产生更强的需求跟更高的粘性，驱动AI汽车真正的像iPhone 4时刻的到来。那么到2026年，我们还将规模量产，支持L4低速场景无人驾驶的车型。我相信当智能驾驶让广大家庭用户信赖，当我们的父母这边也可以放心使用，也可以高频使用的时候，就一定是智能驾驶的真正的成功。
[Company Representative] (XPeng)
Company Representative, XPeng
We're currently undergoing a transformational shift from the era of vehicle electrification to the era of AI. If 2025 marks the beginning of the AI application, then XPeng in-house developed AI vehicles and humanoid robots will be two of the most significant applications of AI in the physical world. I believe that a top AI company should possess cutting-edge full-stack software and hardware capabilities and be able to iterate closed-loop data effectively across large cloud-based AI models, vehicle models, vehicle, electric electronic architecture or EEA, and system on chips or SoC. We expect to begin mass production of our self-developed Turing chip, which by the way, is progressing really well for vehicles, flying cars, and humanoid robots this year. This chip is also designed for swift deployment across global markets and diverse scenarios.
The Turing chip, combined with our full stack in-house developed software and hardware, will enable XPeng to fully leverage scaling law of our vehicles. Our model architecture will not only remain a generation ahead of the industry, but effective parameters used in our vehicles will also be dozens of times larger than those of our competitors, creating a significant gap between us and them. I believe that in the H2 of this year, XPeng will be the first in China to offer a smart driving experience that boasts software capabilities and user experience equivalent to L3 autonomous driving. L3 autonomy will generate strong user demand and exceptional user loyalty, marking an iPhone 4 moment for AI defined cars. Additionally, in 2026, we plan to mass produce vehicle models that will support L4 autonomous driving in low speed scenarios.
True success will be achieved when smart driving earns the trust of a broad range of family users, so even those from my parents' generation can use it confidently and frequently.
He Xiaopeng
Co-founder, Chairman, and CEO, XPeng
一个非常有趣的数据，我们会看到，从今年开始，在中国高等级城区自驾，在中国新购车用户的渗透率将首次突破10%，这意味着自驾需求的拐点会到来，成长曲线将会非线性的向上，这将会给整个的自驾带来巨大的增长机会。那么小鹏在技术、成本、车型的布局都在为快速扩大AI汽车的销量规模，并且推动AI自驾向全球普及做好了准备。从技术上看，我们相信小鹏跟Tesla是全球唯二有能力不依赖于高精地图，不依赖于激光雷达，用一套软件在多个车型实现全球都好用的AI科技的探索。接下来呢，我们期待与全球最好的AI自驾企业在中国跟全球市场同台竞技，推动AI自驾的加速成长。小鹏从P7+开始，所有的新品，包括刚刚上市的2025款G6和G9，都会搭载行业领先的纯视觉AI自驾，并且做到全系标配，无需选装。那么在之后即将上市的MONA M03 Max车型也会首次把城区自驾门槛降低至15万这个级别，让更多年轻用户能够轻松享受科技带来的乐趣。我相信通过将最领先的AI技术跟极致的统一的平台化，平台化跟效率结合，小鹏汽车能够在最宽广的价格带都能够实现AI平权，让广大的用户都能够买得起，也用得好。
[Company Representative] (XPeng)
Company Representative, XPeng
An interesting figure to share with you is that starting from 2025, the penetration rate of advanced urban smart driving among new car buyers in China will exceed 10% for the first time, marking a turning point in the demand for smart driving. This growth trend is expected to be non-linear, presenting a significant opportunity for us. We're well prepared in terms of technology, cost, and model lineup to rapidly ramp up the sales of AI vehicles and promote the global adoption of AI-powered smart driving. From a technology standpoint, XPeng and Tesla are the only two companies worldwide that are capable of providing globally reliable AI smart driving experience without relying on high definition maps or LIDAR, and using a single software suite across the vehicle models.
Going forward, we look forward to competing alongside the world's leading AI autonomous driving companies in both the Chinese and global markets, jointly accelerating the penetration and adoption of AI-driven autonomous driving technologies. 小鹏总以及各位领导，大家晚上好，那首先恭喜本季的这个业绩。那我这边的第一个问题还是跟这个自驾相关，因为目前有看到越来越多的这个车企投入自驾，然后包括也越来越多会慢慢开始用这个端到端大模型，甚至是世界模型，或者是这个VLM等等。那现在的这个环境下，因为有这个AI，或者是包括DeepSeek等等的这种，会不会就是做加速这个training的过程，然后有没有可能把这个第一梯队的这个自驾的这个企业跟这个后面的追赶者，他反而他们有这些tool之后，有些工具之后，跟这个第一梯队的这个技术反而可以稍微拉近。然后另外也想要问一下，就是我们这个图灵芯片的话，它最大的意义，一方面除了降本之外，它对我们目前这个自驾能力的帮助，跟我们现在所使用这个外部供应商的这个芯片，它对我们这个自驾能力的提升可以有多——怎么样的一个体现？那我先翻译我第一个问题。So my first question is still related to autonomous driving, especially right now we are seeing more and more auto companies using end-to-end model or the world model to train their autonomous driving system. So is it possible that the technology gap between the leading AD companies and the companies who are behind to be narrowed?
For XPeng, because you will start to use your Turing chip this year. Besides the cost control, how can this chip help you to advance your AI AD capability? Thank you.
He Xiaopeng
Co-founder, Chairman, and CEO, XPeng
您的第一个问题实际上跟刚刚的第一个问题是有些接近。实际上我尝试把这两个问题合并来讲，我觉得换一个角度，在高等级自动驾驶出现之后，我认为整车厂，特别是拥有全栈自研能力的整车厂，跟之前的包括Tier One或者初步自研能力整车厂的距离会越拉越开。这个整个对于数据闭环迭代的能力，对于研发的能力，对于资本就是盈利，加上使用研发成本的能力，对于全栈的芯片自研跟使用的能力，这些能力会导致的新的高等级自动驾驶厂商拥有要全域的能力，而不是单点就可以突破。它跟在数字世界类似DeepSeek通过开源能够去颠覆很多原来做大模型的公司是有巨大的差异的。那么同时您刚刚问的图灵芯片的问题，对，是一个非常好的问题。我只能讲一个，就是除了在成本上更好之外，当你的模型和你的芯片，和你的芯片开发的工具集都是在你的一个公司体系里面做，你会发现对于能耗，对于性能，对于部分的功能有巨大的提高。这个在之前通过合作芯片也能够去挖掘很多能力，但是没有挖掘如此之大。所以这也是为什么在过去的时间，很多手机厂商他们自研芯片的一个重要的逻辑，它可以取得巨大的领先。所以我相信在将来强AI公司里面，芯片能力、巨大的研发能力、巨大的数据能力，它都是这里面的基础要素之一。谢谢。
[Company Representative] (XPeng)
Company Representative, XPeng
Thank you. Actually, the first part of your question sounded similar to some of the previous questions. I'm gonna respond to both of your questions at once. First of all, after the emergence of high level autonomous driving or smart driving, I believe that for any players in the automotive industry, you will have to have the so-called comprehensive full-stack self development capability. What is that you not only need to have the software capability, but also hardware and also your supply chain capability that allow you to work with the top tier suppliers and also have more and more resources. Having that comprehensive capability is going to draw a bigger advantage for you and create bigger gap between ourselves and our competitors.
Not to mention we have this very powerful data closed loop iteration capability and efficiency, together with our profitability that we are generating right now and also our economies of scale, I believe is going to allow us to be even more competitive than ever before. In addition to that, we also have our self-developed chip and the capability to actually deploy it across multiple scenarios in different markets. That is why we are very confident in our competitive leadership because newcomers or existing incumbents are not easily surpassing us just because they may do better in one aspect or two, which really is very different than the digital competitive landscape, as you mentioned in your question, such as DeepSeek and other AI software company. The second part of your question, this is a very interesting question how the self-developed Turing chip really empower our development for the future?
Let me just give you an example. The reason why so many companies, OEMs or, cell phone, sorry, smartphone, manufacturers try to develop their own chips is because you will realize not only can you gain cost benefits, from developing your own chip, but also it allows you to customize a lot of your products and also have a lot of, potential of development as well. The fact that we are able to self-develop our Turing chip allow us to maintain our leadership. Because we do everything within our own system in the company, you realize that it also allows you to, achieve energy benefits and efficiency and improve your performance of your product significantly.
You also can work with, other players and other suppliers more effectively as well. It allow us to have, the unparalleled self-development capability to also leverage, data and have very effective and fast iteration. That is the reason why, we really, invest heavily in our self-developed Turing chip. Thank you.
Ming-Hsun Lee
Managing Director and Equity Research Analyst, Bank of America
谢谢小鹏总。那第二个问题是关于机器人。我记得之前其实小鹏就已经发布过机器狗，那那时候小鹏总有说过，其实要做出一个性能非常好的机器狗，这难度其实比做出一台性能很好的汽车可能还要更难了。那想要了解一下，就是说，以目前我们现在这个人形机器人的进度，预计2026年，除了量产之外，是不是同时也会商业化？那到目前为止的话，我们这个研发的进度来讲，在哪一些方面是小鹏总目前觉得还比较满意，那哪些还是这个bottleneck，啊，可能是这个成本不够低啊，还是motion control，还是哪些地方？所以说，可能我们还有这个一年多的时间，要把这个短板把它补上。那我也翻译一下我的问题。So my second question is related to the humanoid robot product development. Since you just mentioned that you plan to mass production your humanoid robot in 2026, will you also start to sell the product next year?
Currently based on your development progress, which area you feel you are satisfied? What is the area that you think you still need to continue to make more progress before you officially launch it? 谢谢。
He Xiaopeng
Co-founder, Chairman, and CEO, XPeng
你问了我一个挑战的问题，因为就是涉及到下一代的产品的事情。首先我们的2026年机器人的量产，我们肯定是需要商业化的量产。这个机器人实际上跟造车很不同，而且我认为比造AI汽车要更困难。那么我们看到今天的机器人，在大部分以下半身运动能力很强的机器人，实际上我们认为还是基于L2的能力的。我们认为真正的机器人应该是通用人形的。真正的机器人是需要非常大量真实的数据在糅合模拟的数据的。我们认为机器人比汽车的难度更高，在于包括它是全集成能力。比如说一台AI汽车，它没有AI能力，但是你可以开，但是一个机器人如果没有AI能力，你是不能用的。我们认为它的对于这一个下线的机器人，对于下线能力需要在大量场景是安全、可靠、稳定，可自然语言交互的等一系列这个能力的组合，对于机器人有非常复杂的这个要求，这也是小鹏现在正在做全人形，甚至带有皮肤，带有接近人类关节数量的机器人的原因，这也是小鹏的从去年开始的自动驾驶面向物理世界，同时考虑了为什么架构的体系能够一直做到现在，能够越做越好。我们是考虑的机器人和汽车的自动驾驶能够同源的一整套逻辑。所以，我认为今天我们人形机器人进展是不错的，但是我们也希望先要解决全L3的AI的能力，包括了脚、手、嘴、眼、耳和部分的简单的大脑的AI agent能力的组合，它才是一个可以出街、可以商业的机器人的一个基础的基线。这是我期待能够在以后的时间早一点能够跟大家分享。谢谢。
[Company Representative] (XPeng)
Company Representative, XPeng
Thank you for your question. This is definitely not an easy question to answer because it involves our next generation of technology and products. Now, when we mention the mass production of humanoid robots by 2026, we're definitely talking about the commercial market and large production. When it comes to the manufacturing of humanoid robots, it's actually more challenging than even producing AI vehicles. The reason for that is because it really requires fully integrated capabilities across the board.
Because a true humanoid robot requires not only the hardware, but also real data from our human activities and also simulated data. It's very hard to achieve this comprehensive level of full integration. Right now, when you look at the available products in the market, a lot of our peers are actually focusing on the lower body motion capability of humanoid robot. I believe that is still very limiting because it's restricting themselves to the level two or L2 level capability, which is not enough. For example, if you have an AI vehicle, but you don't fully have the AI capability integrated in it, you can still drive it because it's a car.
A humanoid robot without the AI capability, without that L3 level capability, it's basically useless. Even for the most basic model of the humanoid robot, you still required a lot, including all of the joints that you have for your arm, and also the motion capabilities that you need and the agility that you need, for a robot which is not easy to achieve, when you set the target of achieving the L3 AI capability. Right now what I can share with you is that our humanoid robot R&D is progressing very well, and I believe that what we are able to do right now not only is just the basic lower body capability, but also legs, arms, mouth, and also some very simple, but necessary brain capability.
We call it the agent capability and the combination of basically humanoid or a semi-human brained intelligent capability that we incorporated in our humanoid robot. That is very, very challenging. I hope that in maybe the near future, I can share more update with you when we have more information. Thank you.
Ming-Hsun Lee
Managing Director and Equity Research Analyst, Bank of America
Thank you, President Xiaopeng. That's all my question.
Operator
Our next question comes from Ben Wang with Deutsche Bank.
Ben Wang
Director, Deutsche Bank
谢谢。我有两个问题。第一个想公司给一下一季度的毛利的指引。第二个问题呢，想问也是财务的，想问问看在四季度对比三季度的话呢，长期投的收益呢好像有很大的改善，以及跟滴滴相关的一些账面价值的有很大的改善，为什么在Q4会有一个重回的收益两个亿？我翻译一下。My two questions all about financial.
The first one, can you provide us Q1 gross margin guidance? Second question is about your financial actual improvement in the long-term investment. The other one is the fair value gains which maybe link to the DiDi acquisition. Thank you.
James Wu
VP of Finance and Accounting, XPeng
This is James, I'll answer your question. Yes, so what you've seen, first of all in Q4, is our vehicle margin has improved versus the prior quarter, and this is primarily due to our cost reduction efforts as well as higher scale. As to the forecasting on how to improve our vehicle margin to be standing solidly on the double-digit vehicle margin. Continue to, from a cost front, and as we continue to improve scale, we would benefit from manufacturing cost perspective as well. With regard to your second question on the DiDi related transaction, yes, there was an adjustment that was made. If you recall as we closed the transaction with DiDi, there was an earn-out mechanism that has baked in with DiDi that is linked to the delivery of vehicles registered in the DiDi platform for ride-hailing purposes. Now as we introduce Mona product, we have made decisions internally and obviously align with DiDi, that we are going to focus on the to C customer rather than the to B customer. And therefore, based on our assessment, the first milestone is unlikely to be met, and therefore we have released that liability, which is what you've seen in our financials. Thank you.
Ben Wang
Director, Deutsche Bank
Another was long-term investment.
James Wu
VP of Finance and Accounting, XPeng
We've had some long-term investment revaluations based on our invested companies, and the impact in Q4 is relatively, not significant, I would say. That would come from, some would come from for example the 慧聪投资 we had as an equity holder, and then there are a variety of other investment as well. Overall, the change in Q4 is not as meaningful as what we've seen on the DiDi transaction release.
Ben Wang
Director, Deutsche Bank
Thank you. Very good.
James Wu
VP of Finance and Accounting, XPeng
Thanks。
Operator
Your next question comes from Pingyue Wu with CITIC Securities.
Pingyue Wu
Financial Analyst, CITIC
感谢管理层，我是中信的金融分析师吴平月。那么我这边有两个问题。第一个问题是想请教一下我们的这个海外的业务的进展。因为我们看，因为管理层也提到海外的这个发展正在成为这种长期的这种支柱之一，然后而且从过往的车企的经验，或者是从当前的一种国际环境的角度，可能出海来说是必须，或者以一种形式在海外进行一种生产，或者是一种形式的这种产能合作。所以想请教一下，我们在这种海外的这个产能这个方面，可能我们的进度是怎么样，以及今年的一些出海的这个更细致的规划。 Thank you for the opportunity to ask the question. My first question is about the overseas market. As we can see, the overseas market is one of the pillars for our long-term development. Are we considering to build a factory or some cooperation in terms of capacity overseas? Thank you.
Brian Gu
Vice Chairman and President, XPeng
Hi, it's Brian. Let me address this question. Yes, it's correct that I think international expansion is a key pillar of our growth curve, as He Xiaopeng articulated in the earlier opening speech. We see there is tremendous demand for our high quality technology products for a number of overseas markets. In fact, last year, I think we saw a very encouraging robust reception to our market entries into a number of new markets. By the end of last year, we actually are now selling in over 30 countries globally. In a number of those countries, we saw our product has been positioned as, the top three EV models in the respective categories. I think so far we are very encouraged by the response to our product and technology. In terms of going forward contribution, I think this year we continue to see increased expansion of our global platform.
Our number of stores internationally will double. I think our sales outlets will double from probably roughly 150 to probably over 300 this year. Our number of countries that we're selling our product will close to double as well. We anticipate close to also about doubling of our international sales as a consequence of all these expansion. We also are indeed investing in international infrastructure. We mentioned that we're going to be building.
Overseas R&D centers this year, which will help us to really recruit local talents to focus on international technology development. At the same time, we're also gonna look at a number of local potential production solutions. I think, earlier I think we have jointly announced with our partner in Indonesia to explore local manufacturing production solutions. We'll be also spending time in other regions, so we will obviously share with the market once we actually have these determined. We do have a very detailed and also I would say aggressive plan to make sure that we are well positioned to enter these international markets with the products, with the brand, and also with the local capabilities.
Pingyue Wu
Financial Analyst, CITIC
好，谢谢 Brian。第二个问题我想请教一下关于自驾，然后因为我们今年这个提出的目标是在年底之前达到一个百公里城市接管一次的这么一个计划。那我其实想请教，就是说，如果是对于一个比如说这个 L2++ 的这种功能来说，可能 NPI 等于一百，是不是一个在我们看来一个中远期或中期的一个目标，或者是说我们认为可能 NPI 一百比一百更高，比如说三百甚至是更高，是一个我们的一个极致的一个目标。以及第二个就是说，那我们怎么看，可能对于一些场景，就是车企或者是一些保险公司可能能够去承担一部分这种责任，然后让消费者更好地去、更放心地去使用这种自驾的功能。谢谢。 My second question is about autonomous driving. As we are going to enlarge the NPI to 100 kilometers by the end of this year, do we think it is an ultimate goal for us, or do we aim higher? And also, how do we think of the possibilities for the OEMs or the insurance companies to take some of the responsibilities of the driving systems? Thank you.
He Xiaopeng
Co-founder, Chairman, and CEO, XPeng
关于自动驾驶多少公里接管一次，这是一个在悖论中间向前行的能力。这个话怎么理解呢？也就是说当你的自动驾驶越大范围的覆盖度，比如说能够到小区，到停车场，到所有的小路，那你的自驾的接管率可能越高。当你的用户群越大，因为它就不会像媒体一样，媒体是测试它的极端能力，就是不是到安全，它一般不接管，但是一个普通用户，他可能有安心感，可能有赶时间的效率需求，他会接管。所以从我们车企的角度，是要看车企的大的数据去看。所以今天所有的L2的高阶的自动辅助驾驶都离百公里一次上有不小的距离，包括甚至我们看到的一些L4公司。那么，所以L3是一个巨大的挑战，但是我也相信它只是在下一代的模型，下一代的算力，下一代整车的数据的组合下的一个基础。我认为一个人将来一周甚至一个月开车的距离可能是数百甚至到了两三千公里，如果能够做到能够一周一月只用接管一次两次这样的情况，会推动整个社会的自动驾驶的更高。但是我觉得这是一个……
所以小鹏所说的，我们所说的自动驾驶百公里接管一次，是我们期待的是能够在我们的数据里面能够做到比市场上测试更好的一个效果，这是我们现在的目标，也是我们的L3的初步，我认为它只是初阶，初步阶梯，那么希望将来做到数百甚至数千公里的接管一次。
[Company Representative] (XPeng)
Company Representative, XPeng
Right. Thank you for your question. Now about the human intervention or takeover per 100km. I think this is quite an interesting paradox. We're trying to navigate ourselves within this paradox. The reason for that is because first of all, it depends on the scenarios and the application of the ADAS capability. For example, if you are covering different scenarios, if you are driving within a neighborhood or within a parking lot, the possibility is that you're gonna take over more than let's say if you are just driving on a highway. Also, it depends on who you are and what your purpose is with the testing and calculation of the human intervention, right?
If you are a media, a member of the media, you're going to test the limit of the ADAS capability, which means that you're not gonna take over unless it's absolutely necessary. However, for just an ordinary driver on, for example, daily commute, they might tend to take over more when they feel like it. It really depends. As an OEM, we need to really collect huge amount of data before we can claim that we can achieve, for example, level two or level three ADAS capability or some milestone. When you look at a lot of our peers, even when, they claim that they have L2 plus plus or even L3, L4 capabilities, their hundred kilometers human intervention rate might actually be quite high.
It really depends. I think it is part of our next milestone. Even though achieving L3 capability can be challenging, I still believe that it's achievable, depending on the next generation of model, computing power, and capability and data. With that combination, I believe that, we can actually utilize and leverage ADAS more and more. In the future, perhaps, maybe on a weekly basis or on a monthly basis, we'll be driving maybe hundreds of kilometers or even thousands of kilometers. If we only have to take over maybe once a week, two weeks or once a month, we definitely will promote the whole penetration rate of high level intelligent driving for the whole society. I think this is our goal.
When we mentioned that we need to achieve such a milestone of 1 takeover per 100 kilometers of mileage or driving range, we're actually talking about some measurement of our milestone. Essentially we're talking about the L3 capability that we expect to achieve, and that we believe and we are confident that we can achieve with our capability as well. Also we believe that we are way ahead of the game and we have a higher and more advanced capability than industry average. Thank you. Even for that, let me just add that it's only an initial or an early stage of L3 capability. In the future, maybe we only need to take over every 1,000 kilometers or tens of thousands of kilometers. Thank you.
About the second part of your question, regarding the safety issues of driving and also regulation and related accountability of traffic accidents, we actually have been exploring that very early on, including our proposal during the two sessions of the NPC recently. We have proposed to actually do more so that we can really push the next generation of regulations that can allow us to have more have safer environment of driving. We believe that in this process, China is going to lead the world in becoming a safer environment and having more regulation in this regard. Thank you.
Operator
Your next question comes from Nick Lai with J.P. Morgan.
Charles Zhang
VP of Corporate Finance and Investments, XPeng
技术拐点或者商品拐点，今天我相信没有人能够很清晰地答出来。也许在2026年底到2027年底之间，当我们初步看到有部分人形机器人能够商业化量产之后，大家对这个问题的答案会更相对准确一点。但我觉得现在还属于一个蛮早期的时候，可能处于2010年或者2011年左右的电动汽车的一个时代。在人形机器人，谢谢。
[Company Representative] (XPeng)
Company Representative, XPeng
Thank you. Well, it's very hard to answer your question. I can only say for now is that in the coming 10 years, meaning by 2034, we hope that half of our sales will come from China and the other half will come from the overseas market. We do have our internal plan and targets for 2030, but unfortunately, I have to keep it confidential. The second part of your
The second aspect that I want to mention to respond to your question is regarding humanoid robot. It's very hard to predict when the turning point will come technologically and commercially or, when it comes to the mass production. We might have more visibility by the end of 2026 or end of 2027, when we saw the emergence of mass-produced humanoid robots. I think right now, for now, things are still very foggy. We're probably at about 2010 or, 2011 for new energy vehicles, when it comes to comparing, the humanoid robot development. Thank you.
Nick Lai
Analyst, JPMorgan
好的，非常清楚，谢谢。我第二个问题就是在欧盟政府在两周之前宣布一个新的产业政策，那这个产业政策比较跟咱们相关的就推动智能电动车，然后鼓励外资投资，那这部分因为咱们跟大众有合作，不晓得说在欧盟政府这个新的政策下，我们跟大众合作，目前的产品这个架构是 in China for China，未来有没有可能，就是我们刚刚有提到说我们在海外终于设立这个研发中心，在欧洲市场跟大众这边，在新的产业政策下面，有没有一些新的发展的或合作的机会。My second question is really about the new policy announced by the European government lately on encouraging foreign investment in the European car market, especially on AI autonomous driving cars. And given we have a partnership with Volkswagen, is there any new opportunity we can explore from there?
Thanks。
Charles Zhang
VP of Corporate Finance and Investments, XPeng
Hi, Nick. I think as we laid out our autonomous driving strategy before, I think we're setting up our overseas R&D center, and also we are in the process bringing our autonomous driving technology to the global customers. I think that we are right now setting up the infrastructure to start a preparation. I think in terms of the collaboration with Volkswagen, currently, I think that we are, I think our teams, engineering teams are working really hard to push for the SOP of the G9 platform collaboration as well as the EEA collaboration. We do believe that there is a potential and also the industrial logic to collaborate in the potential overseas market. Thank you.
Operator
That does conclude our Q&A session. I'd like to turn the call back over to the company for closing remarks.
Charles Zhang
VP of Corporate Finance and Investments, XPeng
Thank you once again for joining us today. If you have further questions, please feel free to contact XPeng's investor relations through the contact information provided on our website or the Piacente Financial Communications.
Operator
That does conclude our conference for today. Thank you for participating. You may disconnect your line.

Tina Hou
Equity Analyst, Goldman Sachs
Thanks management for taking my question. My first question is regarding our production preparation for MONA M03. Because previously with G6, I think the supply bottleneck was mainly related to the LIDAR. However, with M03, we don't have LIDAR, so this should have much faster ramp up. Just wondering how much are we preparing for in the next few months. Second question is regarding our R&D expense. We got it for CNY 7 to 7.5 billion previously. Looking at our H1 tracking and looking at last year's H1, H2 seasonality, it seems like it's tracking just below RMB 6 billion. Wondering whether we have any like added R&D spending into the H2. Thank you.
James Wu
VP of Finance and Accounting, XPeng
It's Tina, this is James. I'll try to answer both of your questions.
On Mona, production capacity, obviously we've seen what we have experienced in the past launches with regard to G6 and X9. These are great lessons we've learned. What we have done is we have started preparing the Mona production preparation way ahead of time versus the previous cases. We've anticipated the supply constraints from some of the key components, and we have set sufficient plans to prepare solutions for those issues that we have experienced in the past. So far, we haven't seen any signs of issues with regard to our supply chain and production capacity. We continue to expect we will achieve the planned production and delivery as we have communicated earlier. Your second question about the engineering expense.
Yes, from the H1, if you look at our engineering expenses, it's relatively flat and comparable to last year. As we mentioned earlier, we are entering into a pretty heavy product cycle. A lot of the engineering expenses with regard to design and product development has already kick in. We expect the engineering expenses to ramp up in the H2 of the year. For the full year, we still remain our earlier guidance of about CNY 7 billion for the full year in terms of engineering expense. Thank you.
Tina Hou
Equity Analyst, Goldman Sachs
Thank you. That's very clear.
Operator
Your next question comes from Ping Wu with Haitong International.
Pingyue Wu
Equity Analyst, Citic Securities
Uh,
My first question is, I actually went to see Mona for the first time, and it was of very good quality, but people will only feel the quality when they see the car in person. Do we have some sales action to let more people see the car in person? Yes.
He Xiaopeng
Co-founder, Chairman, and CEO, XPeng
[Foreign language]
[Translator]
Translator
Yes, indeed. Well, when it comes to sales and marketing, technique or approaches, it is quite different between, functional or performance-oriented cars versus, affordable cars. Now, when it comes to Mona, definitely, its capability is more superior to most of the other comparable cars of its class, especially when it comes to aesthetic and dynamic perception capabilities. Since our rollout of the car in, you know, across our different stores since the beginning of August, this year, we've received very unprecedented and very encouraging reception and responses from the consumers, which again, you know, resonates with what you mentioned in your question. You have to see it and feel it, you know, to know how good a car it is.
After our official product launch later this month, we plan to not only do a lot of offline sales and promotional activities, we're also going to do a lot of seeding online as well in order to encourage more customers to test drive it for themselves. We believe that M03's sales performance will be even more superior than G6 of the same comparable sales period.
Also one thing that I would like to add is that, because we are very confident of the performance and capabilities of M03 when it comes to static and dynamic production capability, we believe that once it's launched and officially delivered, word of mouth will serve to our favor, which will also allow more people to become interested in this car and actually test drive it in our dealer shops across the country. Again, you know, there are a lot of sales and marketing possibilities when it comes to promoting this kind of affordable vehicles for the market. Thank you.
Pingyue Wu
Equity Analyst, Citic Securities
[Foreign language] My second question is, we actually do a lot of reform from 2020. After two years, how do we evaluate our ability in sales and marketing right now? Thank you.
He Xiaopeng
Co-founder, Chairman, and CEO, XPeng
[Foreign language]
[Translator]
Translator
Thank you for the question. Two years ago when we started our reform, we started without planning not only when it comes to product launch, but also the planning for the whole you know business, especially in sales and marketing system as well. Then we break it down to our technological development, our sales and marketing system, our customer services. Right now I think we've achieved the first stage of success, where we actually have different aspect of improvement when it comes to our products and also our competitiveness. By 2023, 2024 this year, you will begin to see how it translate into our sales performance.
It's driven not only by our product launch which we prioritize, but also from a comprehensive development of our all rounded capabilities, including what we mentioned previously sales and marketing and also customer services as well. Now right now across the management capabilities, we also focus on developing our store management across tier 2, tier 3, tier 4 cities. We have implemented some new strategies to better serve our customers you know after sales and also when it comes to car insurance etc. We also focus on training our sales staff to improve their overall capability and working efficiency as well. We are very confident of our future development not only in China but also globally speaking. We believe that you know the midterm our target is become you know one of the top players in the China auto making industry when it comes to our sales and marketing capability.
Thank you.
Operator
Your next question comes from Yuqian Ding with HSBC.
Yuqian Ding
Equity Analyst, HSBC
[Foreign language]
My first question is about the gross profit margin. Can management help us to break down the overseas margin and also domestic part, especially the wholesale bits. What's the impact of the profitability over there? If not specific, at least could they give us a little bit reference versus the group average gross profit margin. Also to clarify, Brian said in the H2 of the year roughly the margin level would be mid to low teen percent stay relatively stable. Does that mean the positive benefits of the margin support coming from the software part will largely absorbed by the product mix coming down and also increasing channel discount?
James Wu
VP of Finance and Accounting, XPeng
Yes, this is James. I'll try to answer your question. First, as Brian mentioned, we are expanding on a global basis pretty rapidly, so we would expect the overseas sales, both in terms of absolute volume as well as percentage of total, volume increasing, in the H2 compared to the H1. With regard to margin overseas, in conclusion, it is healthy, good margin. When you look at overseas markets, right, it's quite different when it comes to different countries. And we have different business models in different countries, including, you know, direct sales model, dealership model, as well as distribution model. So the way to understand margin and income, and impact to the bottom line is quite different across these, different models.
In sum, I would say from a variable profit or contribution margin perspective for our overseas business, it is quite good, and it's helping us to improve the overall profitability of the company. All right. Your second question regarding the margin trend in the H2, I just wanted to clarify that, you know, we didn't really refer to the software margin for the H2. What we were talking about earlier was a variety of different components that will come into play in the H2, including higher volume, mix changes, in terms of overseas and domestic, income from the VW collaboration will likely to increase, as well as, you know, additional new vehicle models with regard to Mona and P7+.
Overall, as I mentioned, the margin will maintain and stable in mid to low tens. But from a vehicle margin perspective, we are anticipating, you know, moderate growth, compared to what we've seen in the H1. Thank you.
Yuqian Ding
Equity Analyst, HSBC
Got it.
[Foreign language] So the second question is really about autonomous driving differentiation.
Autonomous driving technology, everyone is developing that, everyone is talking about leveraging the big data loop, engineering capability and processing powers to get it down. But will the industry running into the stage that the technology development curve is running flattish in terms of the development slope? Everyone can do the autonomous driving service, but no one is really sticking out. If we're talking about next year as is the iPhone moment, ChatGPT moment. How could you help us to envision how the singularity and the breakout could happen? Does that mean, because we're getting mature in the technology, so we're selling more vehicle or because of the technology is getting better, we are finding diversified revenue model. Thank you.
He Xiaopeng
Co-founder, Chairman, and CEO, XPeng
[Foreign language]
[Foreign language}
[Translator]
Translator
Well, it will be very challenging for me to try to respond to your questions without involving, you know, technical terms or language, but I'll do my best.
First of all, the previous model or technological approach that was widely adopted industry for ADAS is the so-called all-knowing perspective, relying on high-definition maps and also rule-based architecture to develop their ADAS autonomous driving capability. Now, the main challenge for that approach is that you have actually numerous corner cases where you actually have to examine them one by one, and the customer experience, the driving experience itself is not perfect. For example, most of the ADAS vehicles on the market available right now is driving at about 40 to 50km/h, and also their lane changes and turn making looks very, very robotic. It's not a human-like kind of driving experience.
Whereas the AI approach, or end-to-end AI models approach allow us to actually learn from excellent, and I want to focus on the executive here, excellent or high quality experienced driver, or human-like driver, someone like yourself, you know, when it comes to the driving habit and the performance across different areas of the country. Obviously, they also encountered a challenge of solving different corner cases because it's not rule-based. For example, if you encounter stray animals, for example, a stray cat in the world, you know, on the road, it's not going to try to avoid it because it's not something that they've learned before. Whereas in a rule-based approach, maybe there is a rule there that states that you have to avoid hitting those animals. There are pros and cons to different approaches.
I believe the development of the capabilities based on this AI end-to-end model is going to be a lot more significant and a lot quicker than the previous rule-based approach. I hope I answered your question. Thank you.
Operator
That does conclude our question and answer session. I'd like to turn the call back over to the company for closing remarks.
Alex Xie
Head of Investor Relations and Capital Markets, XPeng
Thank you once again for joining us today. If you have further questions, please feel free to contact XPeng's Investor Relations team via the contact information provided on our website for the Piacente Financial Communications. Thank you.
Operator
This concludes today's conference call. You may now disconnect your line. Thank you.
